To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the subjective preference for each pitch detection algorithm depends on the pitch range of speaker and the transmission condition of recording.
the performance of a pitch detector is a function of the speaker, transmission environment, and speech material.

(1) the pitch detection algorithms that were found to have good objective performance were also found to have good subjective performance, (2) the subjective preference for each of the seven pitch detection algorithms was found to be a function of both speaker and transmission environment, (3) the preference for each pitch detection algorithm was found to be consistent across the eight listeners, and (4) the preference for the semiautonomously determined pitch contour was not significantly different from that of any of the seven pitch algorithms

a subjective evaluation of the performance of seven LPC based pitch detectors.
the development and evaluation of pitch detectors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a pitch detector that is optimal in one environment or for one type of speaker is not optimal in another environment or for another type of speaker.
the performance of the pitch detection algorithms is highly dependent on the type of error that one is willing to tolerate.

the pitch detectors perform well in terms of their objective performance, but the results of the subjective evaluation indicate that some of these algorithms may not be suitable for use in speech synthesis.

the subjective evaluation is not a simple reflection of the objective performance evaluation.
the performance of pitch detectors is highly dependent on the type of speech used for evaluation.
a subjective evaluation of pitch detectors is a useful supplement to an objective evaluation of pitch detection algorithms.
